title: Ethylene–isobutane to n-octane
summary: A simplified Aspen Plus V11 flowsheet with a stoichiometric reactor, flash separation, a distillation column and a recycle-and-purge loop.
content:
I built this model to practise how separate pieces of equipment behave together in a plant. Fresh ethylene (100 kmol/h) and isobutane (50 kmol/h) are mixed with the recycle stream, heated, and sent to an RStoic reactor operating at 10 bar. The reactor effluent is cooled and flashed at 20 °C and 10 bar. The liquid goes to a 15-stage RadFrac column (feed on stage 3); the overhead is split 95% recycle and 5% purge, and the bottoms is the n-octane product.

The reaction is the simplified stoichiometry 2 C2H4 + C4H10 → C8H18, with an ethylene conversion of 80% specified in the reactor block. Property method: Peng–Robinson.
results: n-octane product of about 49.74 kmol/h at the base case.
Reboiler duty near 1192.7 kW, heater near 514.7 kW and condenser near −233.65 kW.
The feed (100 kmol/h ethylene, 50 kmol/h isobutane) is exactly stoichiometric, so the most octane it can make is 50 kmol/h.
limitations: The reactor uses a specified 80% conversion, not reaction kinetics, and the reaction is a simplified representation that has not been validated against experimental data. Results also depend on the property method, recycle configuration and separation specifications.
